[[Oil terminal]] | revenue = {{increase}} $57.342 billion (2022) | net_income = {{increase}} $1,037 billion (2022) | assets = {{decrease}} $23.892 billion (2022) | equity = {{increase}} $13.325 billion (2022) | website = {{URL|https://www.plains.com/}} | footnotes = {{cite web | url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/0001070423/000107042323000006/paa-20221231.htm | title=Plains All American Pipeline, L.P. 2022 Form 10-K Annual Report | publisher=[[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]]}} }} '''Plains''' (also known as "'''Plains All American Pipeline, L.P."''' and "'''Plains GP Holdings'''") is a [[master limited partnership]] engaged in [[pipeline transport]], marketing, and storage of [[liquefied petroleum gas]] and [[petroleum]] in the [[United States]] and [[Canada]].{{Cite web |title=Who We Are |url=https://www.plains.com/who-we-are/ |access-date=2025-12-22 |website=Plains All American Pipeline |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Plains GP Holdings |url=https://fortune.com/company/plains-gp-holdings/ |access-date=2025-12-22 |website=Fortune |language=en}} Plains owns interests in {{convert|18,370|mi|km}} of pipelines, storage capacity for about 75 million barrels of crude oil, 28 million barrels of NGLs, 68 billion cubic feet of [[natural gas]], and 5 [[natural gas processing]] plants. The company is headquartered in the [[Allen Center]] in [[Downtown Houston]], [[Texas]]. Plains (NASDAQ: PAA) is a publicly traded [[Master limited partnership]]. PAA owns an extensive network of pipeline transportation, terminalling, storage and gathering assets in key crude oil and NGL producing basins and transportation corridors at major market hubs in the United States and Canada.{{Cite web |title=About Us |url=https://www.plains.com/about-us |access-date=July 30, 2023 |website=Plains}} ==History== The company began in 1981 as a small oil and gas exploration and production company called Plains Resources.{{cite web | url=https://www.plainsallamerican.com/about-us/company-history | title=Company History | publisher=Plains All American Pipeline, L.P.}} It became a [[publicly traded company]] via an [[initial public offering]] in 1998. Major acquisitions include: * 1998 - All American Pipeline System * 1999 - [[Scurlock Oil Company]] Permian and west Texas pipeline from [[Chevron Corporation]] for $35 million{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/houston/stories/1999/07/12/daily11.html | title=Plains Scurlock acquires crude oil pipeline | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=July 16, 1999}} * 2001 - CANPET Energy Group, a liquified gas marketing company based in Canada, for $42 million{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/houston/stories/2001/04/09/daily11.html | title=Plains All American to buy CANPET Energy Group | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=April 11, 2001}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/companies/article/17263154/plains-all-american-buys-canadian-crude-lpg-marketer | title=Plains All American buys Canadian crude, LPG marketer | work=[[Oil & Gas Journal]] | date=April 11, 2001}} * 2004 - Rainbow oil pipeline in Northern Alberta{{cite news | url=https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/companies/article/17269607/plains-all-american-to-buy-canadian-rainbow-oil-pipeline | title=Plains All American to buy Canadian Rainbow oil pipeline | work=[[Oil & Gas Journal]] | date=April 10, 2008}} * 2012 - The combined system includes ~5,500 miles of pipeline, ~6.8 million barrels per day of pipeline capacity, and ~16.9 million barrels operational storage capacity.{{Cite web |date=July 27, 2023 |title=Plains All American |url=https://www.plains.com/about-us/company-history |website=Plains All American Pipeline, L.P.}} * 2025 - [[Diamondback Energy|Diamondback Energy, Inc]] and Kinetik Holdings Inc. - operators of the EPIC Crude Oil Pipeline.{{Cite web |last=Warren |date=2025-09-13 |title=Plains All American to buy majority of EPIC Crude Pipeline |url=https://energiesmedia.com/plains-to-buy-majority-of-epic-crude-pipeline/ |access-date=2025-12-22 |website=energiesmedia.com |language=en-US}} ==Financial performance and credit ratings== The company earned a profit in nine of the ten calendar years from 2013 to 2022. It reported a $2.59 billion loss for calendar year 2020. Management attributed the 2020 loss to the COVID-19 global pandemic, which reduced demand for energy products. ===2010 settlement=== In 2010, the company agreed to pay a $3.25 million civil penalty for violating the [[Clean Water Act]] and to spend $41 million to upgrade more than 10,000 miles of crude oil pipelines after the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency]] pressed charges regarding 10 pipeline spills in Texas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, and Kansas between June 2004 and September 2007 that spilled over 273,000 gallons of crude oil, some of which ended up in rivers, lakes, and oceans.{{cite web | url=https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/plains-all-american-pipeline-settlement | title=Plains All American Pipeline Settlement | publisher=[[United States Environmental Protection Agency]] | date=August 10, 2010}} ===Little Buffalo oil spill=== The [[2011 Little Buffalo oil spill]] was one of the largest land-based oil spills in North America, the largest [[oil spill]] in Alberta in 36 years, and the second spill in Alberta within a two-week period. The Rainbow Pipeline system, owned by Plains Midstream Canada, ruptured on April 29, 2011, spilling 28,000 barrels of oil in a fairly isolated stretch of [[boreal forest]] in northern [[Alberta]], about four miles from the nearest homes in [[Little Buffalo, Alberta]].{{cite news | last=Welsch | first=Edward | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748704322804576303440805617516 | title=Size of Oil Spill in Canada Grows | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=May 5, 2011 | url-access=subscription}}{{Cite news | last=Vanderklippe | first=Nathan | url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/costs-for-oil-companies-pile-up-after-spill/article578815/ | title=Costs for oil companies pile up after spill | work=[[The Globe and Mail]] | date=May 4, 2011}} The local school was closed due to concerns about the effects of fumes.{{cite news | url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/industry-news/energy-and-resources/location-of-oil-spill-near-little-buffalo-alta/article634637/ | title=Location of oil spill near Little Buffalo, Alta | work=[[The Globe and Mail]] | date=May 4, 2011}} The incident resulted in charges against the company in 2013.{{Cite news | url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/2nd-largest-pipeline-spill-in-alberta-history-leads-to-charges-1.1311723 | title=2nd largest pipeline spill in Alberta history leads to charges | work=[[CBC News]] | date=April 26, 2013}} In 2013, the [[Energy Resources Conservation Board]] of Alberta reprimanded the company for operational failures in connection with the oil spill.{{cite news | url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/calgary/plains-midstream-reprimanded-for-2011-alberta-oil-spill-1.1311724 | title=Plains Midstream reprimanded for 2011 Alberta oil spill | work=[[CBC News]] | date=February 26, 2013}} ===Rangeland Pipeline Incident=== Heavy rains in early June 2012 caused a leak on a 46-year-old Plains Midstream Canada pipeline at Jackson Creek, Alberta, a tributary of the [[Red Deer River]], which spilled approximately 1,000-3,000 barrels of light sour crude into the Red Deer River. {{cite news | url=https://financialpost.com/commodities/energy/alberta-pressured-to-include-leaks-in-environmental-monitoring-plan | first=Bob | last=Weber | title=Alberta pressured to include leaks in environmental monitoring plan | work=[[Financial Post]] | date=June 14, 2012}}{{cite news | url=https://www.pressreader.com/canada/calgary-herald/20120616/281840050743111 | title=Calls growing for probe of aging pipeline system: Recent spills highlight ongoing risk | work=[[Calgary Herald]] | first=Stephen | last=Ewart | date=June 16, 2012}} The company was charged in 2014.{{Cite news | url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/plains-midstream-charged-in-red-deer-river-pipeline-spill-1.2662309 | title=Plains Midstream charged in Red Deer River pipeline spill | date=June 2, 2014}} ===Refugio oil spill=== {{main|Refugio oil spill}} On May 19, 2015, a pipeline operated by the company ruptured northwest of [[Santa Barbara, California]].{{cite news | last=Cooper | first=Lara | title=Oil Spill Reported on Coast Near Refugio State Beach | url=https://www.noozhawk.com/article/oil_spill_reported_on_coast_near_refugio | work=[[Noozhawk]] | date=May 19, 2015}} Within 24 hours, oil polluted approximately 9 miles of the Santa Barbara coast. The spill shut down the popular [[El Capitán State Beach]] and Campground during [[Memorial Day]] weekend, just prior to the beginning of the summer high season. The spill leaked {{convert|105,000|USgal|oilbbl}}, including {{convert|20,000|USgal|oilbbl}} that reached the [[Pacific Ocean]].{{cite news | last=Hayden | first=Tyler | title=As Refugio Oil Slick Spreads, Spill Estimate Rises | url=https://www.independent.com/2015/05/20/refugio-oil-slick-spreads-spill-estimate-rises/ | work=[[Santa Barbara Independent]] | date=May 20, 2015}}{{cite magazine | last=Frizell | first=Sam | title=California Governor Declares State of Emergency After Santa Barbara Oil Spill | url=https://time.com/3891739/california-oil-spill-jerry-brown-state-of-emergency/ | magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] | date=May 20, 2015}} The [[United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce]] opened an investigation into the oil spill on June 25, 2015. Companies are required to report to the [[National Response Center]] on the release of hazardous-material "at the earliest practicable moment."; however, the company did not initially report the spill.{{cite news | url=https://www.post-gazette.com/business/powersource/2015/06/27/California-oil-spill-gushed-like-hose-without-a-nozzle-3/stories/201506270145 | title=California Oil Spill Gushed Like Hose 'Without a Nozzle' | publisher=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] | agency=[[Associated Press]] | date=June 26, 2015}} According to preliminary findings of the federal [[Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration]] released in June 2015, corrosion had worn a pipeline section to less than an inch thick. By June 2015 the cost of cleanup rose to USD$92 million. Santa Barbara County firefighters were among the first to discover the spill, before being notified by the company, and they "built a rim of rocks to prevent oil from running to the shoreline."{{cite news | url=https://www.independent.com/2015/05/28/supes-gently-grill-feds-over-refugio-spill-response/ | title=Supes Gently Grill Feds over Refugio Spill Response County Asks for Timeline; Plains Mum on 'Emergency Response Plan' | first=Kelsey | last=Brugger | work=[[Santa Barbara Independent]] | date=May 28, 2015}}{{cite web | url=https://calspillwatch.wildlife.ca.gov/Spill-Archive/Refugio | title=Refugio Incident, Santa Barbara County, May 19, 2015 | publisher=[[California Department of Fish and Wildlife]]}} In March 2020, the company agreed to pay over $60 million in penalties related to the incident.{{cite press release | url=https://www.epa.gov/newsreleases/us-pipeline-company-modify-its-national-operations-implement-safeguards-resulting-oil | title=U.S. Pipeline Company to Modify Its National Operations to Implement Safeguards Resulting from Oil Spill | publisher=[[United States Environmental Protection Agency]] | date=March 13, 2020}} === Byhalia Connection pipeline === In December 2019, the company announced a joint venture with [[Valero Energy|Valero Energy Corp]]. to build the Byhalia Connection pipeline – a crude oil pipeline system that would run 49 miles from Memphis to Marshall County, Mississippi,{{Cite web|last=Macaraeg|first=Sarah|title=What you need to know about the Byhalia Connection pipeline in Memphis|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/news/2021/03/23/byhalia-pipeline-memphis-what-you-need-know-environmental-justice/4772256001/|access-date=2021-07-08|website=The Commercial Appeal|language=en-US}} and connect two existing crude oil pipelines: the [[Diamond Pipeline|Diamond pipeline]] and the Capline pipeline.{{Cite web|title=About the Project|url=https://byhaliaconnection.com/about-project/|access-date=July 8, 2021|website=Byhalia Connection}} Concerns over the pipeline's route through the Memphis Sand aquifer, as well as the city's predominantly Black neighborhoods, sparked an opposition movement. The struggle to stop the pipeline gained widespread attention, with environmental and social justice advocates like [[Jane Fonda]] and [[Danny Glover]] lending their support.{{Cite web|last=Macaraeg|first=Sarah|title=What you need to know about the Byhalia Connection pipeline in Memphis|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/news/2021/03/23/byhalia-pipeline-memphis-what-you-need-know-environmental-justice/4772256001/|access-date=2021-07-08|website=The Commercial Appeal|language=en-US}} Former Vice-President [[Al Gore]] called the pipeline a “reckless, racist rip-off,”{{Cite web|title=Black Community in Memphis Defeats Oil Pipeline That Threatened Water Supply|url=https://www.democracynow.org/2021/7/6/headlines/black_community_in_memphis_defeats_oil_pipeline_that_threatened_water_supply|access-date=2021-07-08|website=Democracy Now!|language=en}} and U.S. Rep. [[Steve Cohen (politician)|Steve Cohen]] asked President [[Joe Biden]] to consider revoking the project's federal permit.{{Cite web|last=Watts|first=Micaela A.|title=Cohen asks Biden to deny Byhalia pipeline permit; Danny Glover, other celebrities voice opposition|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/news/2021/02/22/celebrities-ask-biden-deny-byhalia-connection-pipeline/4540677001/|access-date=2021-07-08|website=The Commercial Appeal|language=en-US}} After defending the pipeline and then putting its planned construction on hold in May 2021, the company announced on July 2, 2021 that it was abandoning the project.{{Cite news|title=Company drops plans for Byhalia pipeline; Activists rejoice: 'Sometimes the good guys win'|language=en-US|work=The Commercial Appeal|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/news/2021/07/02/plains-all-american-abandons-plan-byhalia-connection-oil-pipeline-memphis/7848508002/|access-date=2021-07-08}} Community leader Justin J. Pearson called the pipeline’s cancellation an “extraordinary testament to what Memphis and Shelby County can do when citizens build power toward justice.”{{Cite web|title=Black Community in Memphis Defeats Oil Pipeline That Threatened Water Supply|url=https://www.democracynow.org/2021/7/6/headlines/black_community_in_memphis_defeats_oil_pipeline_that_threatened_water_supply|access-date=2021-07-08|website=Democracy Now!|language=en}} ==References== {{Reflist|1}} ==External links== {{Portal|Energy|Companies|Texas}} * {{Official website|https://www.plainsallamerican.com/}} {{Finance links | name = Plains All American Pipeline, L.P. | google = PAA | yahoo = PAA | bloomberg = PAA:US | reuters = PAA | sec_cik = PAA | nasdaq = PAA }} [[Category:1981 establishments in Texas]] [[Category:1998 initial public offerings]] [[Category:American companies established in 1981]] [[Category:Companies based in Houston]] [[Category:Companies formerly listed on the New York Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Nasdaq]] [[Category:Energy companies established in 1981]] [[Category:Natural gas pipeline companies]] [[Category:Oil companies of the United States]] [[Category:Oil pipeline companies]] [[Category:Payne County, Oklahoma]] [[Category:Petroleum in Oklahoma]] [[Category:Non-renewable resource companies established in 1981]]
